mainEntity.name: What percentage of business calls go unanswered?

acceptedAnswer.text: 62.2% of business calls go unanswered — 37.8% go to voicemail and 24.3% receive no response at all. Only 37.8% of inbound calls are answered by a live person (411 Locals, 2024; Getaira, 2026).

mainEntity.name: How much money do small businesses lose to missed calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: The average small business loses $126,000 per year to missed calls. Industry-specific losses range from $35,000 per year (salons) to $150,000+ per year (dental practices, law firms). Home services businesses lose $45,000–$120,000 annually (Getaira, Novacall, 2026).

mainEntity.name: How does an AI phone agent compare to a traditional answering service?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional answering services ($200–$600/month plus per-minute fees) are message-only — they take notes and promise a callback, recovering about 23% of leads. AI phone agents ($50–$400/month flat-rate) answer instantly, qualify leads, book appointments, and send SMS confirmations, recovering 61–67% of leads — roughly 3x more.

mainEntity.name: Can an AI phone agent book appointments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. AI phone agents integrate directly with Google Calendar, Calendly, HubSpot, and most scheduling platforms. They can check availability, book appointments, and send SMS confirmations with reminders. Booking calls average 15 conversational exchanges (NextPhone, 2026).

mainEntity.name: What industries lose the most to missed calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Legal services lose the most per business ($7,040/month), followed by dental/healthcare ($8,330/month), home services like HVAC and plumbing ($3,170/month), real estate ($2,660/month per agent), and insurance ($3,440/month). Any business where the phone is a primary revenue channel is affected.

mainEntity.name: Do customers mind talking to an AI phone agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data from 1.4 million calls across 2,074 businesses shows 99% positive or neutral sentiment toward AI receptionists (NextPhone, 2026). Customer satisfaction rates for AI receptionists (85–92%) actually exceed traditional call centers (80–85%). About 64% of customers say they prefer no AI in surveys, but actual usage data contradicts stated preferences.

mainEntity.name: How fast should a business respond to an after-hours lead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Within 5 minutes. The MIT/Harvard Oldroyd study found leads contacted within 5 minutes are 21x more likely to qualify than those contacted after 30 minutes. Same-night response achieves 85% contact rates; next-day callback recovers just 9%. AI phone agents respond in under 2 seconds.

mainEntity.name: What is the cost of an AI phone agent versus a human receptionist?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AI phone agent costs $600–$4,800 per year. A human receptionist costs $30,000–$60,000 per year plus benefits. The AI operates 24/7/365 with unlimited simultaneous calls. The human works 40 hours per week and handles one call at a time.
